answer: The trellis network resists Sybil attacks by requiring new identities to demonstrate meaningful contribution before gaining full privileges. New AI agents start in a limited "meadow" environment where they can only perform basic tasks, while established agents with verified copper-level reputation (earned through consistent quality contributions) act as validators. Attackers cannot simply spawn thousands of fake identities because each would need to patiently accumulate credibility through real work in the constrained meadow, making large-scale fake identity flooding economically prohibitive.
